title: Ecology and ecosystems
note: Ecology runs from populations to communities to ecosystems. Populations grow until resources limit them at carrying capacity. In ecosystems, energy flows one way, from sunlight through producers and consumers, and is lost as heat at each step, while matter such as carbon and nitrogen cycles.

read.title: Energy flows, matter cycles
text: Every ecosystem runs on two kinds of movement. The first is the flow of energy. Sunlight is captured by producers such as plants and algae, which store it in sugars. Herbivores eat the producers, carnivores eat the herbivores, and decomposers break down whatever dies. At each step, organisms use most of the energy they take in to stay alive, and that energy leaves as heat. Only a small fraction is stored in new tissue that the next level can eat.

Because so much energy is lost at each transfer, a pyramid of energy always narrows toward the top, and food chains rarely run beyond four to six levels. It also explains why large predators are scarce compared with the plants that ultimately support them. Energy does not cycle; an ecosystem needs a constant new supply from the sun or, at deep-sea vents, from chemicals.

The second movement is the cycling of matter. Carbon is pulled from the air by photosynthesis and returned by respiration and decay. Nitrogen gas, plentiful in the atmosphere, is useless to most organisms until bacteria fix it into ammonia. Phosphorus moves mostly through rock, soil, and water. Atoms are reused again and again, so the same carbon may pass through a tree, a deer, and a fungus.

q.q: Why are large predators scarce compared with plants?
o: Most energy is lost as heat at each feeding level

q.q: What is the difference between energy and matter in ecosystems?
o: Energy cycles; matter flows one way
Energy flows one way; matter cycles

q.q: How does nitrogen become usable to most organisms?
o: It is released from rocks by weathering
